name: Puka

spells.name: Bane
spells.text:
You fill the minds of your enemies with doubt. Enemies in the area must succeed at a Will save or take a –1 status penalty to attack rolls as long as they are in the area. Once per round on subsequent turns, you can Sustain the spell to increase the emanation's radius by 10 feet and force enemies in the area that weren't yet affected to attempt another saving throw.

Bane can counteract Bless.

Spell Effect: Bane

spells.name: Bullhorn
spells.text:
You amplify your voice, loud enough for you to be heard easily at a great distance. For the duration, your voice can be heard loudly and clearly by all listeners within 500 feet, even if other ambient noise would otherwise block the sound. Despite the volume, this doesn't make your voice jarring or distracting. This doesn't increase the range or area of other auditory or linguistic effects, and physical barriers such as walls and doors still block or muffle your voice as normal.

Your loud voice makes it easier to Coerce others, and the acoustics assist in Performing at a large venue. You gain a +1 status bonus to checks to Coerce and auditory Performance checks to Perform at a large venue. You can Dismiss the spell.

Spell Effect: Bullhorn

---
Heightened (5th) Your voice can be heard clearly up to 1,200 feet away.

Heightened (7th) Your voice can be heard clearly up to 1 mile away.

spells.name: Frostbite
spells.text:
An orb of biting cold coalesces around your target, freezing its body. The target takes 2d4 cold damage with a basic Fortitude save. On a critical failure, the target also gains weakness 1 to bludgeoning until the start of your next turn.

Spell Effect: Frostbite

---

Heightened (+1) The damage increases by 1d4 and the weakness on a critical failure increases by 1.

spells.name: Gust of Wind
spells.text:
A violent wind issues forth from your palm, blowing from the point where you are when you Cast the Spell to the line's opposite end. The wind extinguishes small non-magical fires, disperses fog and mist, blows objects of light Bulk or less around, and pushes larger objects. Large or smaller creatures in the area must attempt a Fortitude save. Large or smaller creatures that later move into the gust must attempt the save on entering.

---

Critical Success The creature is unaffected.

Success The creature can't move against the wind.

Failure The creature is knocked Prone. If it was flying, it takes the effects of critical failure instead.

Critical Failure The creature is pushed 30 feet in the wind's direction, knocked prone, and takes 2d6 bludgeoning damage.

spells.name: Wall of Shrubs
spells.text:
You call forth a line of bushes native to the region to spring from the ground. The wall of shrubs stands in a line 60 feet long, is less than 5 feet tall, and is a foot thick, providing lesser cover.

---

Heightened (3rd) The shrubs are 10 feet tall and 5 feet thick, provide standard cover, are difficult terrain, and have a Climb DC of 15. The duration increases to 10 minutes.

Heightened (5th) As 3rd rank, but the shrubs provide greater cover and the duration is 1 hour. You can choose to form a ring of shrubs with a diameter of up to 30 feet instead of a line.

items.name: Unknowable Truth
items.text: Except when transformed with Change Shape, a puka is invisible and intangible, able to move through the Universe but unable to interact with physical objects or creatures except to speak. Even then, a creature must succeed at a DC 20 Perception check check to hear an invisible puka's voice.

items.name: Change Shape
items.text:
The puka takes on the appearance of one of the following creatures: a Tiny fox, hare, house cat, or raven; a Small dog, goat, or humanoid (most often a gnome or goblin); a Medium wolf or humanoid (most often an elf or human); or a Large horse. The humanoid shapes always include minor animalistic features. The puka keeps their normal Strikes, though their hoof strike deals slashing damage instead of bludgeoning in shapes with claws.

---

items.name: Wild Bolt
items.text: The puka Strides five times. They can't use Wild Bolt again for 1d4 rounds.

items.name: Wild Ride
items.text:
Frequency once per day

Requirements The puka is invisible or in the shape of a horse, and is not in an encounter

---
Effect The puka bursts into a run. Their land Speed becomes 90 feet until an hour passes, they stop moving, they enter an encounter, or they take damage, whichever comes first. Moving at this Speed nonstop for the full hour, the puka can typically cover 20–30 miles. If the puka bears a rider, that rider can't move from their mounted position or be harmed in any way until the Wild Ride ends. An unwilling rider can attempt to get off as soon as the puka starts moving, but must succeed at a DC 20 Acrobatics check check or Reflex save.

text:
A puka's true form is unknown to all, save perhaps the Eldest. These private and tricksy shapeshifters almost always wear another shape, and they're invisible when not transformed. Pukas most commonly appear as fine black horses with golden eyes, often in full tack, approaching unsuspecting mortals and enticing them to take a ride. When a puka succeeds in coaxing a rider onto their back, they launch into a gallop far faster than any horse could sprint, taking their unfortunate rider on a wild and terrifying—but ultimately harmless—journey before dropping them off exactly where they were picked up. They play similar pranks in their other forms: leading hunters on a merry chase through darkened woods as a fox or wolf, tempting late-night tavern goers as a beautiful humanoid, or taunting mortal animals as an uncatchable hare.

Any animal form a puka takes is covered in slick black fur. Even in their humanoid guises, their hair remains similarly shiny and dark, and they always include some tell-tale animalistic features, such as a horse's ears or a fox's tail.
